boards.title: Your First Weekend at St. Mary's College of Maryland, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence for getting oriented across campus, its waterfront, and the adjacent historic site.

cards.title: Start by finding the campus hub
cards.subtitle: Campus Center · Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the Campus Center as your first landmark: check posted Student Activities events, orient yourself to the building, and choose a simple meeting point.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the campus hub and its student-life programming.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM identifies the Campus Center as the hub of student life and a place for movies, lectures, and Student Activities events.
cards.access_notes: Check the College events calendar or Student Activities postings for any current program details.

cards.title: Have an early meal in the Great Room
cards.subtitle: Campus Center, second floor · Friday evening
cards.notes: Meet your new floor or classmates for a meal, then use the Campus Center location to map the walk back to your residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining stop that doubles as an easy rendezvous point.
cards.evidence_claim: The Great Room is SMCM's main dining hall, located on the second floor of the Campus Center.
cards.access_notes: Dining uses a meal plan or payment; consult the current dining menu and hours before going.

cards.title: Locate the library before you need it
cards.subtitle: Across from the Campus Center · Saturday morning
cards.notes: Walk over from the Campus Center, find the circulation desk, and identify a floor or study area you can return to during the first week.
cards.short_summary: A practical orientation stop for research help and future study time.
cards.evidence_claim: Hilda C. Landers Library & Archives is across the path from the Campus Center and is Building 23 on the SMCM campus map.
cards.source_title: Directions and Maps | Hilda C. Landers Library & Archives
cards.access_notes: Library staff can direct visitors from the circulation desk; confirm building access and service hours locally.

cards.title: Take a daytime waterfront walk
cards.subtitle: St. Mary’s River · Saturday late morning
cards.notes: Head to the river in daylight for the beach, dock, and shoreline views; keep the visit simple and follow waterfront safety guidance and posted conditions.
cards.short_summary: See the riverfront setting that anchors campus recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM describes its waterfront as a place to relax on the beach, swim in the St. Mary’s River, or launch a kayak or paddleboard.
cards.access_notes: SMCM states students have free daily access to recreational waterfront equipment; use only under current College rules and conditions.

cards.entity_name: Michael P. O’Brien Athletics & Recreation Center
cards.title: Tour the ARC’s recreation options
cards.subtitle: MPOBARC · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Stop in to locate the fitness areas, pools, courts, and climbing wall, then ask staff how student recreation access and any required orientation work.
cards.short_summary: Get the lay of the land for indoor fitness and recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: The ARC includes a climbing wall, Aquatics Center, fitness and weight-training areas, recreational courts, and an arena.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current student access procedures, pool availability, and equipment requirements with the facility.

cards.title: Pause at the Greens
cards.subtitle: By the townhouses · Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or simply sit for a while at this townhouse-side communal lawn; it is a useful reset before making evening plans with new friends.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor communal space beside the townhouses.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM describes The Greens by the townhouses as a communal space for relaxing and identifies The Pillow there as a sitting area.
cards.access_notes: Use the shared outdoor space respectfully and follow any residence-life or event-use notices.

cards.title: Check for the weekend movie
cards.subtitle: Campus Center · Saturday evening
cards.notes: Look for the current film listing, bring a few classmates, and make this an easy indoor evening plan if a screening is scheduled that weekend.
cards.short_summary: A simple campus movie option for a group evening.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM says students can catch free movies at Cole Cinema every weekend.
cards.access_notes: Verify the current screening title and start time through College event listings before going.

cards.title: Cross Route 5 for local history
cards.subtitle: Adjacent historic site · Sunday morning
cards.notes: Set aside time for the reconstructed buildings and exhibits next door, and begin at the visitor center so you can choose the areas that fit your time.
cards.short_summary: Explore Maryland’s first capital at the site beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM describes Historic St. Mary’s City as a nearby site with exhibits, reconstructed buildings, and staff interpretation; SMCM students receive complimentary exhibit admission tickets.
cards.access_notes: Historic St. Mary’s City lists Tuesday–Saturday hours of 10 a.m.–4 p.m. for 2026; obtain the College ticket and confirm exhibit availability.

cards.title: End with a quiet river overlook
cards.subtitle: Near Kent Hall · Sunday afternoon
cards.notes: Take a short reflective pause by the garden and river before the week starts; use the path and seating gently, especially if an event is being set up.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped campus site overlooking the St. Mary’s River.
cards.evidence_claim: SMCM says the Garden of Remembrance is near Kent Hall, overlooks the St. Mary’s River, and was dedicated in 1934.
cards.access_notes: The Garden is also an event space; respect reservations, signage, and any setup activity.

cards.entity_name: Commemorative to Enslaved Peoples of Southern Maryland
cards.title: Make time to learn and reflect
cards.subtitle: SMCM campus · Sunday before sunset
cards.notes: Approach this outdoor memorial as a reflective visit: read the interpretation, move through the site thoughtfully, and leave enough time for the history to register.
cards.short_summary: An immersive campus memorial centered on the lives of enslaved people.
cards.evidence_claim: The College identifies the Commemorative as an immersive art experience honoring enslaved people who once lived in St. Mary’s City.
cards.access_notes: The College lists visiting hours as Monday–Sunday, sun-up to sundown.
